enzyme_name: unresolved step of the TDP-L-megosamine pathway (megalomicin deoxysugar cluster)
organism_context: Micromonospora megalomicea (megalomicin producer); reconstituted in E. coli
rationale: The written step (dTDP-2,6-dideoxy-3-keto-L-hexose <-> dTDP-L-megosamine) is a legacy lumped entry with no cofactors and no surviving KEGG reaction; in vivo reconstitution shows TDP-L-megosamine is built from TDP-4-keto-6-deoxy-D-glucose by five separate enzymes (MegBVI, MegDII, MegDIII, MegDIV, MegDV), so no single protein catalyses it. Each of those is a standalone single-activity deoxysugar-tailoring enzyme; none is reported as a fusion.
direction_note: Physiologically this is a committed nucleotide-sugar biosynthetic step running toward dTDP-L-megosamine (the LLM council's '>'); ModelSEED's '<' points back up the pathway, and the equation is missing the amino donor and SAM, so the dGP/GC calls are made on an unbalanced reaction.

enzyme_name: no enzyme assigned (maltol release from dTDP-3,4-dioxo-2,6-dideoxy-D-glucose)
organism_context: actinomycete dTDP-deoxysugar pathways (KEGG map00523)
rationale: KEGG R06443 (dTDP-3,4-dioxo-2,6-dideoxy-D-glucose -> maltol + dTDP) carries no EC number and no orthology, and two literature searches returned no characterised catalyst; maltol is generally treated as a non-enzymatic elimination/aromatisation shunt product of the 3,4-diketo deoxysugar intermediate.
direction_note: The elimination releases dTDP and aromatises to maltol, which is irreversible (the LLM's '>'); ModelSEED has additionally dropped the dTDP leaving group, so the equation is mass-unbalanced and the +557/+446 kJ/mol dG estimates are meaningless.

enzyme_name: unassigned C-2 deoxygenation of dTDP-4-keto-L-rhamnose
organism_context: actinomycete polyketide sugar unit biosynthesis (KEGG map00523)
rationale: KEGG R06445 (dTDP-4-dehydro-beta-L-rhamnose <-> dTDP-4-oxo-2,6-dideoxy-L-mannose) lists neither an EC number nor an orthology group; the chemistry is a C-2 deoxygenation, which in characterised pathways needs a dTDP-sugar 2,3-dehydratase plus a 3-ketoreductase (two separate proteins), so the single written step has no identifiable catalyst.
direction_note: C-2 deoxygenation in dTDP-deoxysugar assembly is an irreversible dehydration/reduction pair running toward the 2,6-dideoxy sugar (the LLM's '>'); ModelSEED's '<' would re-hydroxylate C-2, which no enzyme does.

enzyme_name: pikromycin modular type I polyketide synthase (PikAI-PikAIII plus thioesterase)
organism_context: Streptomyces venezuelae; 10-deoxymethynolide is the 12-membered lactone released after module 5 (PikAIII) with the PikAIV thioesterase
rationale: The Pik PKS is explicitly four multifunctional polypeptides, each a covalent chain of KS/AT/ACP plus KR, DH and ER domains, terminating in a thioesterase that macrolactonises the chain; this is a textbook polyfunctional megasynthase, not a loose complex.
direction_note: Chain extension is decarboxylative and chain release is an irreversible thioesterase-catalysed macrolactonisation, so flux can only run precursors -> 10-deoxymethynolide (the LLM's '>'); ModelSEED's '<' would depolymerise the macrolactone back to acyl-CoAs, which no enzyme does.

enzyme_name: pikromycin modular type I polyketide synthase (PikAI-PikAIV)
organism_context: Streptomyces venezuelae; narbonolide is the 14-membered lactone released by the full PikAI-PikAIV assembly line
rationale: Same megasynthase as rxn04319 run to six extension modules: four multifunctional polypeptides each carrying several distinct catalytic domains on one chain, ending in the PikAIV thioesterase.
direction_note: Decarboxylative extension plus irreversible thioesterase macrolactonisation fix the direction toward narbonolide (the LLM's '>'); the ModelSEED '<' direction is chemically impossible for a PKS.

enzyme_name: hydroxycinnamoyl-CoA: anthocyanin 3-O-glucoside-6''-O-acyltransferase (anthocyanin 3-O-glucoside p-coumaroyltransferase, 3AT)
organism_context: Perilla frutescens (red form); BAHD acyltransferase superfamily, homologues across anthocyanin-acylating angiosperms
rationale: The cloned Perilla enzyme is a single-activity BAHD acyltransferase that transfers p-coumaroyl from its CoA thioester to the 6''-OH of the anthocyanin 3-O-glucose; no second catalytic activity is reported for it or for its BAHD relatives.
direction_note: Acyl transfer is driven by cleavage of the coumaroyl-CoA thioester and runs toward the acylated anthocyanin (the LLM's '>'); ModelSEED's equation has dropped p-coumaroyl-CoA and CoA entirely, so the dGP/GC disagreement is on a stripped, unbalanced reaction rather than on the real acylation.

enzyme_name: hydroxycinnamoyl-CoA: anthocyanin 3-O-glucoside-6''-O-acyltransferase (3AT), acting on cyanin to give shisonin
organism_context: Perilla frutescens; shisonin is the 3-O-(6-O-p-coumaroyl)glucoside-5-O-glucoside of cyanidin, i.e. the 3AT product of cyanin
rationale: Same monofunctional BAHD acyltransferase as rxn04399 - it coumaroylates the 3-O-glucose of cyanidin 3,5-di-O-glucoside (cyanin) to give shisonin; a single acyl-transfer activity, no second catalytic function reported.
direction_note: Thioester-driven acylation toward shisonin (the LLM's '>'); the ModelSEED equation again omits the p-coumaroyl-CoA/CoA pair, which is why the two dG sources split.

enzyme_name: chalcone synthase (naringenin-chalcone synthase, EC 2.3.1.74) acting together with the separate chalcone reductase polypeptide (6'-deoxychalcone synthase system, EC 2.3.1.170)
organism_context: legumes and other 5-deoxy(iso)flavonoid producers (Glycyrrhiza, Medicago, Glycine, Morus)
rationale: Isoliquiritigenin (6'-deoxychalcone) formation needs two distinct proteins - the homodimeric type III PKS chalcone synthase and the aldo-keto reductase chalcone reductase - which is a two-protein system, not a fused chain, so per protocol CHS is scored monofunctional; CHS's iterative condensation plus cyclisation/aromatisation all occur in one active site and count as a single activity. ModelSEED's combined 1.3.1.-/2.3.1.74 annotation reflects the two-protein pairing, not one bifunctional enzyme.
direction_note: Three decarboxylative condensations plus NADPH-dependent reduction make chalcone formation effectively irreversible (the LLM's '>'); the ModelSEED equation has lost 3 malonyl-CoA, NADPH, 4 CoA and 3 CO2, leaving a bare 4-coumaroyl-CoA <-> isoliquiritigenin pair that both dG sources score as a huge positive, which is an artefact of the truncation.

enzyme_name: 3-amino-5-hydroxybenzoate (AHBA) synthase RifK, acting in complex with RifL as the UDP-3-keto-D-glucose:L-glutamate aminotransferase
organism_context: Amycolatopsis mediterranei and other ansamycin producers; the unrelated Bacillus subtilis kanosamine route instead uses the dedicated monofunctional sugar aminotransferase NtdA on glucose 6-phosphate
rationale: The same PLP polypeptide performs two chemically distinct reactions: as a homodimer it aromatises 5-deoxy-5-amino-3-dehydroshikimate to AHBA (the last pathway step), and in a complex with the oxidoreductase RifL it transaminates UDP-3-keto-D-glucose (the first step) - KEGG K16016 accordingly carries both EC 4.2.1.144 and 2.6.1.-. The RifL partnership is a complex, but the two catalytic activities sit on the one RifK chain.
direction_note: A bifunctional enzyme that works at both ends of the same pathway is exactly the kind of case that confuses a direction heuristic: the transamination half is near-equilibrium but is pulled toward UDP-kanosamine by the committed downstream steps (the LLM's '>'), while ModelSEED's '<' reads the step as deamination. The equation also omits the L-glutamate/2-oxoglutarate pair.

enzyme_name: unassigned release of free kanosamine from UDP-kanosamine (KEGG K16017, AHBA-synthesis-associated protein)
organism_context: Amycolatopsis mediterranei rifamycin / aminoshikimate pathway
rationale: KEGG R06587 has no EC number and attaches only an uncharacterised 'AHBA synthesis associated protein'; the reviewed aminoshikimate pathway describes kanosamine being phosphorylated downstream by RifN but does not name the enzyme that liberates it from the UDP-sugar, and no biochemical characterisation was found.
direction_note: Hydrolytic release of a sugar from a UDP-sugar is strongly exergonic and one-way toward free kanosamine (the LLM's '>'); ModelSEED's '<' would require UDP capture without UDP in the equation, which is also why it is unbalanced.

enzyme_name: 3,5-dihydroxyphenylacetyl-CoA synthase (DpgA), a type III polyketide synthase (EC 2.3.1.246)
organism_context: Amycolatopsis orientalis / Streptomyces toyocaensis and other glycopeptide (vancomycin, teicoplanin) producers
rationale: DpgA was expressed and assayed as a standalone type III PKS that condenses four malonyl-CoA into 3,5-dihydroxyphenylacetyl-CoA; the accessory DpgB (isomerase) and DpgD (dehydratase) that accelerate it are separate polypeptides, so this is a multi-protein system rather than a fused bifunctional enzyme.
direction_note: Four decarboxylative condensations make the reaction irreversible toward DPA-CoA (the LLM's '>'); ModelSEED has lost one malonyl-CoA plus 3 CoA and 4 CO2, so the ~+1300 to +1700 kJ/mol dG figures reflect the truncation, not the real step.

enzyme_name: dTDP-4-keto-L-vancosamine 4-ketoreductase (VcaE; EvaE in the chloroeremomycin epi-vancosamine pathway)
organism_context: Amycolatopsis orientalis (vancomycin/chloroeremomycin); KEGG assigns R06630 to K18836, reductase VcaE
rationale: In the fully reconstituted TDP-L-epi-vancosamine pathway the five Eva proteins each carry out exactly one chemical step, with EvaE (VcaE homologue) performing only the terminal NADPH-dependent C-4 ketoreduction; no second catalytic activity is reported on this SDR chain.
direction_note: The NADPH-dependent ketoreduction is the last committed step of TDP-L-vancosamine synthesis and runs toward the reduced sugar (the LLM's '>'); ModelSEED keeps only '2 H+' and has lost the NADPH/NADP+ pair, so even the eQuilibrator value (+12.2 kJ/mol, graded silver) is scoring a mis-specified half-reaction.

enzyme_name: auraviketone/aklaviketone reductase (anthracyclinone 7-ketoreductase, EC 1.1.1.362)
organism_context: Streptomyces galilaeus (auramycin/aclacinomycin); characterised representative is DauE of Streptomyces sp. C5 (daunomycin), the same KEGG orthologue K15944
rationale: Recombinant DauE catalyses only the NADPH-specific C-7 ketoreduction, converting aklaviketone, maggiemycin and 7-oxodaunomycinone to the corresponding anthracyclinones; it is a single-activity ketoreductase with no second catalytic function reported, and the auramycinone reaction is run by the same orthologue.
direction_note: This is an NADPH-driven reduction that commits the aglycone, so the physiological direction is auraviketone -> auramycinone (the LLM's '>'); ModelSEED's equation retains only '2 H+' with NADPH/NADP+ stripped out, which is why eQuilibrator's apparently confident +12.0 kJ/mol points the wrong way.

enzyme_name: aklanonic acid methyltransferase (S-adenosyl-L-methionine:aklanonate O-methyltransferase, DnrC; EC 2.1.1.288)
organism_context: Streptomyces peucetius (daunorubicin), Streptomyces sp. C5, Streptomyces galilaeus (aclacinomycin)
rationale: Bioconversion with the cloned gene showed DnrC does one thing - methylate aklanonic acid to aklanonic acid methyl ester - and it is a small standalone SAM-dependent O-methyltransferase; contrast the genuinely bifunctional anthracycline enzyme RdmB (methyltransferase-fold hydroxylase), which is a different protein acting later in the pathway.
direction_note: SAM-dependent methyl transfer is strongly exergonic and physiologically one-way toward the methyl ester (the LLM's '>'); ModelSEED's '<' would require SAH-driven demethylation, which DnrC does not perform, and eQuilibrator's sentinel uncertainty (23901 kJ/mol) means it supplies no usable constraint here.

enzyme_name: aklaviketone reductase (aklavinone 7-ketoreductase, DauE/DnrE; EC 1.1.1.362)
organism_context: Streptomyces sp. strain C5 and Streptomyces peucetius (daunorubicin/doxorubicin); KEGG orthologue K15944
rationale: DauE was cloned and shown in extracts to carry out the NADPH-specific reduction of aklaviketone to aklavinone (and of maggiemycin and 7-oxodaunomycinone); neither DauB nor the neighbouring polyketide ketoreductase has this activity, so it is a dedicated single-activity enzyme.
direction_note: NADPH-dependent reduction to aklavinone is the committed biosynthetic direction (the LLM's '>'); the ModelSEED equation has lost NADPH/NADP+ and shows only '2 H+', so eQuilibrator's silver-graded +12.0 kJ/mol is computed on the wrong reaction.

enzyme_name: daunorubicin C-13 ketoreductase (DnrU)
organism_context: Streptomyces peucetius; KEGG assigns R06694 to K15956
rationale: dnrU was cloned and characterised as the ketoreductase that reduces the C-13 ketone of daunorubicin to 13-dihydrodaunorubicin, and its disruption raises doxorubicin titre; it is an aldo-keto-reductase-family single-activity enzyme with no second catalytic function reported.
direction_note: DnrU runs reductively (daunorubicin -> 13-dihydrodaunorubicin, the LLM's '>'), but note this is an off-pathway shunt rather than a committed biosynthetic step, so neither direction is strongly constrained physiologically; the ModelSEED equation also keeps only '2 H+' with NADPH/NADP+ stripped.

enzyme_name: (S)-DNPA enoyl reductase ActVI-ORF2
organism_context: Streptomyces coelicolor A3(2), actinorhodin pathway; KEGG lists only 'enoyl reductase' (K14628/K14629) for R06695
rationale: Recombinant ActVI-ORF2 was shown in vitro to reduce (S)-DNPA stereospecifically to 6-deoxydihydrokalafungin using NADPH, and is described as a discrete enoyl reductase; a single catalytic activity, with no fused second domain.
direction_note: NADPH-dependent enoyl reduction is physiologically unidirectional toward DDHK (the LLM's '>'); the ModelSEED equation has lost NADPH/NADP+ and keeps only '2 H+', so the eQuilibrator '<' call is on a mis-specified reaction.

enzyme_name: unassigned late step of medermycin biosynthesis (dihydrokalafungin -> medermycin)
organism_context: Streptomyces sp. AM-7161 (med biosynthetic gene cluster)
rationale: KEGG R06698 carries neither an EC number nor an orthology group; converting dihydrokalafungin into the C-glycoside medermycin requires at least a C-glycosyltransferase plus the angolosamine deoxysugar machinery of the med cluster, most of whose ORFs remain uncharacterised, so no single catalyst corresponds to the written step.
direction_note: C-glycosylation from an NDP-sugar is effectively irreversible in the biosynthetic direction (the LLM's '>'); ModelSEED's equation omits the sugar donor entirely, so neither dG source is scoring the real transformation.

enzyme_name: cocaine synthase (benzoyl-CoA:methylecgonine benzoyltransferase, EcCS), a BAHD acyltransferase
organism_context: Erythroxylum coca and E. novogranatense
rationale: KEGG R06727 (benzoate + 1-methylpyrrolinium -> cocaine) is a placeholder with no EC and no catalyst; the real terminal step is run by cocaine synthase, a single-activity BAHD acyltransferase that esterifies methylecgonine with benzoyl-CoA (it also accepts cinnamoyl-CoA, which is the same activity on a different substrate, not a second one). Confidence is low because the written lumped reaction spans several further enzymes besides EcCS.
direction_note: The genuine step is a thioester-driven acyl transfer that runs toward cocaine (the LLM's '>'); the lumped KEGG/ModelSEED form substitutes free benzoate for benzoyl-CoA and omits the pyrrolidine-to-tropane chemistry, so the thermodynamic estimates here are not evaluating any real enzyme reaction.

enzyme_name: pseudoecgonine--CoA ligase (uncharacterised acyl-CoA synthetase, EC 6.2.1.-)
organism_context: KEGG tropane/pyridine alkaloid map rn00960; no organism or protein assigned
rationale: KEGG R06731 carries only the partial EC 6.2.1.- with no orthology group and no named protein, and no literature characterisation of a pseudoecgonyl-CoA synthetase was found; the class assignment alone does not identify a protein, so functionality cannot be judged.
direction_note: ATP-dependent acyl-CoA ligases are pulled forward by pyrophosphate hydrolysis, so thioester formation (the LLM's '>') is the physiological direction; ModelSEED's equation omits the diphosphate product, leaving it unbalanced and the dG estimate unusable.

enzyme_name: pyrrolidine ketide synthase (PYKS/AbPyKS), a type III polyketide synthase; the decarboxylation to hygrine itself is non-enzymatic
organism_context: Atropa belladonna, Anisodus acutangulus, Datura stramonium; Erythroxylum carries a homologous PYKS
rationale: PYKS condenses N-methyl-delta-1-pyrrolinium with malonyl-CoA to 4-(1-methyl-2-pyrrolidinyl)-3-oxobutanoate, and the loss of CO2 to hygrine (which is what KEGG R06732 actually writes) is a spontaneous non-enzymatic step; PYKS is a single-activity type III PKS. Scored monofunctional for the PKS, with the caveat that no enzyme catalyses the decarboxylation itself.
direction_note: Beta-keto-acid decarboxylation is irreversible toward hygrine (the LLM's '>'); ModelSEED has dropped malonyl-CoA and CO2, reducing the step to a 1-methylpyrrolinium <-> hygrine pair that cannot balance, which is why GC and dGPredictor disagree in sign.

enzyme_name: unassigned slaframine pathway segment (L-pipecolate -> slaframine)
organism_context: Rhizoctonia (Slafractonia) leguminicola, the red-clover black-patch fungus
rationale: KEGG R06742 has no EC number and no orthology; labelling studies show pipecolate is elaborated to slaframine through several steps (condensation with a malonate-derived C2 unit, cyclisation, reduction, amination and a terminal 1-O-acetylation), and none of the individual enzymes has been purified or sequenced, so the written lumped step has no identifiable catalyst.
direction_note: L-pipecolate is the committed precursor and flux runs toward slaframine (the LLM's '>'); ModelSEED's '<' amounts to degrading the alkaloid back to pipecolate, for which no activity is described.

enzyme_name: NovR (CloR in clorobiocin), the bifunctional non-heme iron oxygenase of aminocoumarin ring A biosynthesis
distinct_activities: oxidative decarboxylation/hydroxylation of 3-dimethylallyl-4-hydroxyphenylpyruvate, an alpha-keto acid, incorporating two oxygen atoms
oxidative decarboxylation of the 3-dimethylallyl-4-hydroxymandelate intermediate, an alpha-hydroxy acid, incorporating one oxygen atom
organism_context: Streptomyces roseochromogenes DS 12976 (CloR, characterised) and Streptomyces spheroides/niveus (NovR, novobiocin)
rationale: The purified enzyme is reported as a bifunctional non-heme iron oxygenase that performs two mechanistically distinct consecutive oxidative decarboxylations on one polypeptide, taking 3DMA-4HPP via 3DMA-4-hydroxymandelate to 3DMA-4-hydroxybenzoate. Note KEGG's R06762 writes an aldehyde intermediate that does not match the characterised route, so the ModelSEED step is an approximation of the first CloR/NovR half-reaction.
direction_note: Both half-reactions consume O2 and release CO2, so the enzyme is strictly unidirectional toward the oxidised ring A precursor (the LLM's '>'); ModelSEED's equation omits O2 and CO2, which is why GC and dGPredictor split on sign.

enzyme_name: decarbamoylnovobiocin 3''-O-carbamoyltransferase (NovN, EC 2.1.3.12)
organism_context: Streptomyces spheroides (S. niveus), novobiocin producer; homologue CouP in coumermycin
rationale: NovN was overexpressed, purified and shown to carbamoylate only the 3''-OH of five different decarbamoyl aminocoumarins, and has been crystallised as a standalone O-carbamoyltransferase; a single catalytic activity (contrast the iteratively acting but still single-activity CTase GdmN).
direction_note: Carbamoyl transfer is driven by release of inorganic phosphate from carbamoyl phosphate and is the final, irreversible tailoring step of novobiocin assembly (the LLM's '>'); ModelSEED's '<' would have novobiocin regenerate carbamoyl phosphate, which NovN does not do, and eQuilibrator's sentinel uncertainty (23901 kJ/mol) gives no real constraint.

enzyme_name: unassigned anatabine formation from nicotinic acid-derived units
organism_context: Nicotiana tabacum and related species
rationale: rxn04594 has no EC number, no xrefs and no named catalyst; anatabine is formed in tobacco by condensation of two nicotinic-acid-derived 3,6-dihydronicotinic acid units, a coupling widely regarded as at least partly non-enzymatic (the analogous nicotine coupling was only recently resolved enzymatically), so no enzyme can be assigned to the written step.
direction_note: In planta flux runs from nicotinic acid toward anatabine, which accumulates as an end product (the LLM's '>'); ModelSEED's '<' implies anatabine catabolism back to niacin, for which no route is described, and the written 1:1 stoichiometry is wrong because two pyridine units condense.
